quests.title: The Floral Courtyard: Part III

dialogue.t: In the following days, I will continue to stay here and guide those who come for the Irodori Festival, and help them to enjoy the beauty of the "floral courtyards."
Don't forget to drop by every day to get another "theme." There will be a total of four such themes for you to figure out.
Of course, if you have any other questions, I will do my best to answer them for you.

dialogue.sit: I have no further questions at the moment.

dialogue.t: The flowers I use are all provided by Sakuya's Flowers. The flowers they grow are of impeccable quality and affordable prices.
Perhaps you've met Sakuya as well. We once studied ikebana under the same master.

Sakuya is also very well-studied in the floral arts, but when she heard that there would be tons of people at the Irodori Festival, she seemed to have gotten a bit of stage fright. She said that it would be difficult to quiet down and focus on her work in such an environment.
In any case, I will advertise Sakuya's Flowers on her behalf.
We can help too if you need us!
Well then, do the two of you have any other questions?
Think nothing of it. If you have time, you can come and look for me any time.
Ah, it's you two. Right on time, I'd say.
After two rounds of practice, your understanding of the floral arts has truly increased by leaps and bounds.
As such, I've made some small changes to today's theme to perhaps help open up a new line of thought for your consideration.
Uhh, you say that, but Paimon's suddenly getting kinda nervous.
Hehe, there's no need to fret. Just relax. Relax...
Considering your talent, I believe that you merely need to give the theme due consideration.

dialogue.sit: You flatter us, but do go ahead.
I've got some other things to do at the moment...

dialogue.t: In that case, today's theme is "the jade leaves do repose, the flowers are born in the wind."
I wonder what answer the two of you will give...

quests.description: Amidst the Irodori Festival, the florist Fushizome is looking for someone to experience the art of ikebana.
